stem.text: The Boltzmann distribution of the particles in a mixture of gas X and gas Y is shown in diagram 1.

stem.alt: Diagram 1: Boltzmann distribution curve, percentage of particles against energy. The curve starts at the origin, rises to a single maximum, then falls gradually.

stem.text: X and Y react and the reaction causes an increase in gas molecules present. The reaction goes to completion.

In experiment 1, the increase in volume is measured every 10 seconds. During the reaction, the temperature and pressure remain constant. The increase in volume is shown in the volume–time graph in diagram 2.

stem.alt: Diagram 2: volume-time graph, increase in volume in cm3 against time in s. The curve starts at the origin, rises steeply then levels off at a constant volume.

stem.text: In experiment 2, the experiment is repeated using identical amounts of X and Y. A different temperature is used compared to experiment 1. The same pressure is used. The Boltzmann distribution of the second mixture of X and Y is shown in diagram 3. During the reaction the temperature and pressure remain constant.

stem.alt: Diagram 3: Boltzmann distribution curve, percentage of particles against energy. The peak is lower in energy and taller than in diagram 1, and the curve falls more steeply after the peak.

stem.text: Which curve on the volume–time graph would show the increase in volume against time for experiment 2? (The original line for experiment 1 is redrawn as a solid line.)

stem.alt: Volume-time graph, increase in volume in cm3 against time in s, with four curves labelled A, B, C and D. The solid curve B is the experiment 1 line. A dashed curve A rises fastest to the highest plateau, dashed curve B rises fast to the same plateau as the solid line, dashed curve C rises slowly to the same plateau as the solid line, and dashed curve D rises slowly to a lower plateau.
